mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk aversion, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during a global supply chain shock.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that erodes real corporate earnings and compresses valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during a synchronized global growth shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related earnings and confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during a period of strong mortgage rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating growth in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k for three consecutive months, coinciding with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200k for three consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 10% signals a shift from consumption to savings, which reduces near-term demand and pressures cyclically sensitive sectors, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during a fiscal stimulus rollout.
